canonical_data: JSON scan state with a backup copy and a living plan of clusters, queue order, and dispositions under a .desloppify directory in the scanned project
strengths: Only items explicitly queued appear in the execution queue, and resolving or skipping work needs an explicit action rather than a quiet scan
Mechanical detectors across 29 languages and a scoring design meant to resist gaming, where wontfix items widen the gap between the lenient and strict scores
Scan state is written atomically with a backup and a recovery path, so progress carries across sessions
weaknesses: Licensed under the custom Open Source Native License 0.2: internal use is free, but shipping it inside a product by a company that is not open source falls into paid tiers

Three quarters of the score comes from LLM review of subjective dimensions, so results vary with the reviewing model and the README's claim that a score above 98 matches a beautiful codebase is the author's own
The agent does the fixing through the host's own tools; Desloppify supplies the queue, scoring, and instructions rather than an agent loop of its own
The most recent commit is from May 2026
why_it_matters: Shows a host-installed workflow that earns its place through owned state and a gated queue, giving coding agents a measurable, resumable code-health loop instead of one-shot cleanup prompts.
